A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TOP-ERL and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The retained content and additions can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated robot-learning experiments on Meta-World, Hopper Jump, and Box Pushing, including baseline comparisons and ablations in Figures 4–6 and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports individual Meta-World task curves, longer Box Pushing curves, and a trajectory example.

M1.justification: The Transformer critic, N-step targets, policy objective, ProDMP initialization, TRPL, and random segmentation remain unchanged. Appendices A.1–A.2 explain retained components and reference-policy options without establishing a change to the implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 50 Meta-World tasks, Hopper Jump, and dense- and sparse-reward Box Pushing. The individual Meta-World plots in v2 disclose results within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain TCE, BBRL, PPO, GTrXL trained with PPO, gSDE, SAC, and PINK. The critic-target variants in Figure 5 and Table 1 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 4c–d extends TOP-ERL's reported training/evaluation horizon from approximately 14 million interactions in v1 to 40 million in v2. The task definitions, evaluation metrics, and hyperparameter Tables 4–7 remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether runs were continued or repeated.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 and Figure 7 add a concrete Box Pushing trajectory example contrasting an unconditioned new trajectory with five segments initialized at the old trajectory's states. The performance ablations, segmentation sensitivity experiment, and action-correlation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight random seeds, interquartile means, and 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. The additional curves do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice or an increased seed count.

E6.justification: Figures 8–9 add individual learning curves for all 50 Meta-World tasks and their baselines, substantially expanding the reported results beyond the existing aggregate. Figure 4 also revises and extends TOP-ERL's Box Pushing curves to approximately 40 million interactions. Table 1 and the aggregate Meta-World and Hopper Jump curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds explicit constrained optimization definitions for the per-state mean and covariance projections in Eq. (11). Appendix B.3 removes v1's final xi-based trajectory expansion and coefficient definitions while retaining the underlying initial-condition solution. The core objectives and ODE mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution list and the conclusion retain the same claims about off-policy episodic learning, Transformer sequence-value estimation, sample efficiency, and performance across 53 tasks. The abstract edits do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 adds the interpretation that varying segment lengths regularizes critic training by exposing the V-function to Q-targets over different action horizons. The limitations concerning within-episode changes and POMDPs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository hyperlink and a reproducibility statement covering implementations, environments, and trained models. Appendices A.1–A.2 disclose Cholesky-based sampling, TRPL projection details, and behavior-policy or EMA reference choices. These expand documentation; the existing hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Agrawal et al. (2019) and Schulman et al. (2015) in the TRPL discussion. Section 4 more explicitly distinguishes inherited trajectory-generation and stabilization techniques from the proposed critic and update mechanisms, while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose corrections, clarifies Section 4 headings, expands Appendix A into three subsections, and adds Appendix B.4 plus acknowledgments, ethics, and reproducibility statements. The main narrative structure remains intact. Appendix A.1 introduces incorrect section and equation references.

P2.justification: The new trajectory Figure 7 and two figures containing 50 individual task panels substantially expand the visual presentation. Figure 4 is relocated, retained appendix figures are renumbered, and hyperparameter tables receive increased vertical spacing.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through individual Meta-World results and longer Box Pushing curves, and improves reproducibility documentation through fuller explanations of policy training and TRPL plus a code link. These are useful additions to an otherwise stable method and evaluation. Incorrect cross-references in Appendix A.1 introduce small presentation defects, but the added clarity and inspectable evidence support a limited net improvement.
